concept.title: Manage conflicts between node and machine health checks
concept.shortdesc: When both, node health checks and machine health checks are deployed, the node health check avoids conflict with the machine health check.

note.p: Red Hat OpenShift deploys machine-api-termination-handler as the default MachineHealthCheck resource.

conbody.p: The following list summarizes the system behavior when node health checks and machine health checks are deployed:

ul.li: If only the default machine health check exists, the node health check continues to identify unhealthy nodes. However, the node health check ignores unhealthy nodes in a Terminating state. The default machine health check handles the unhealthy nodes with a Terminating state.

conbody.codeblock: INFO MHCChecker ignoring unhealthy Node, it is terminating and will be handled by MHC {"NodeName": "node-1.example.com"}

ul.li: If the default machine health check is modified (for example, the unhealthyConditions is Ready), or if additional machine health checks are created, the node health check is disabled.

conbody.codeblock: INFO controllers.NodeHealthCheck disabling NHC in order to avoid conflict with custom MHCs configured in the cluster {"NodeHealthCheck": "/nhc-worker-default"}

ul.li: When, again, only the default machine health check exists, the node health check is re-enabled.

conbody.codeblock: INFO controllers.NodeHealthCheck re-enabling NHC, no conflicting MHC configured in the cluster {"NodeHealthCheck": "/nhc-worker-default"}
